items.title: The Cause of Generation: Craving Moistens the Seed

items.zh: 依有潤種子因依處，施設生起因。所以者何？由欲、色、無色界繫法，各從自種子生。愛名能潤，種是所潤。由此所潤諸種子故，先所牽引各別自體當得生起。如經言：業為感生因。愛為生起因。是故依有潤種子依處，施設生起因。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of the moistened seed that the cause of generation is set forth. Why is this? Because phenomena bound to the desire realm, the form realm, or the formless realm each arise from their own seed. Craving is what moistens; the seed is what is moistened. Because of these seeds thus moistened, the individual body previously impelled comes to actually arise. As the sūtra says: karma is the cause of the destiny attained, craving is the cause of its actual arising. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of the moistened seed, the cause of generation is set forth.

items.title: The Cause of Inclusion: Every Other Supporting Condition

items.zh: 依無間滅因依處，及依境界、根、作用、士用、真實見因依處，施設攝受因。所以者何？由欲繫諸法無間滅攝受故，境界攝受故，根攝受故，作用攝受故，士用攝受故，諸行轉。如欲繫法如是，色、無色繫法亦爾。或由真實見攝受故，餘不繫法轉。是故依無間滅、境界、根、作用、士用、真實見依處，施設攝受因。
items.en: It is with reference to the loci of uninterrupted cessation, and of an object, a faculty, function, human effort, and genuine insight, that the cause of inclusion is set forth. Why is this? Because it is through being included by uninterrupted cessation, through being included by an object, a faculty, function, and human effort, that phenomena bound to the desire realm proceed to operate. As with phenomena bound to the desire realm, so too with those bound to the form or formless realms. And it is through being included by genuine insight that the remaining, unbound phenomena proceed to operate. It is for this reason that, with reference to the loci of uninterrupted cessation, an object, a faculty, function, human effort, and genuine insight, the cause of inclusion is set forth.

items.title: The Cause of Drawing-Forth: How a Small Good Grows Into a Great One

items.zh: 依隨順因依處，施設引發因。所以者何？由欲繫善法，能引欲繫諸勝善法。如是欲繫善法，能引色、無色繫及不繫善法。由隨順彼故。如欲繫善法，如是色繫善法能引色繫諸勝善法，及無色繫善法、不繫善法。如色繫善法，如是無色繫善法能引無色繫諸勝善法，及不繫善法。如無色繫善法，如是不繫善法能引不繫諸勝善法，及能引發無為作證。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of conformity that the cause of drawing-forth is set forth. Why is this? Because a wholesome quality bound to the desire realm can draw forth a still more excellent wholesome quality bound to the desire realm. So too, a wholesome quality bound to the desire realm can draw forth a wholesome quality bound to the form or formless realms, or unbound to any of the three. As with a wholesome quality bound to the desire realm, so a wholesome quality bound to the form realm can draw forth a still more excellent wholesome quality bound to the form realm, as well as a wholesome quality bound to the formless realm or unbound to any realm. As with a wholesome quality bound to the form realm, so a wholesome quality bound to the formless realm can draw forth a still more excellent wholesome quality bound to the formless realm, as well as an unbound wholesome quality. As with a wholesome quality bound to the formless realm, so an unbound wholesome quality can draw forth a still more excellent unbound wholesome quality, and can even draw forth the direct realisation of the unconditioned.

items.zh: 又不善法能引諸勝不善法。謂欲貪能引瞋、癡、慢、見、疑、身惡行、語惡行、意惡行。如欲貪，如是瞋、癡、慢、見、疑，隨其所應盡當知。如是無記法能引善、不善、無記法，如善、不善、無記種子阿賴耶識。又無記法能引無記勝法。如段食能引受生有情令住、令安，勢力增長。由隨順彼故。是故依隨順依處，施設引發因。
items.en: Further, an unwholesome quality can draw forth a still more forceful unwholesome quality. That is: craving for desire can draw forth hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, and misconduct of body, speech, and mind. As with craving for desire, so too hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and doubt should each be understood, in due accordance, to draw forth the rest. So too a neutral quality can draw forth a wholesome, an unwholesome, or a neutral quality, just as the ālayavijñāna, itself neutral, contains wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral seeds alike. Further, a neutral quality can draw forth a still more excellent neutral quality — as edible food can sustain, comfort, and strengthen a being taking rebirth. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of conformity, the cause of drawing-forth is set forth.

items.title: The Cause of Fixed Distinction: Barley Seed Never Sprouts Wheat

items.zh: 依差別功能因依處，施設定異因。所以者何？由欲繫諸法自性功能有差別故，能生種種自性功能。如欲繫法，如是色、無色繫及不繫法亦爾。是故依差別功能依處，施設定異因。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of differentiated capacity that the cause of fixed distinction is set forth. Why is this? Because phenomena bound to the desire realm, having differences in their own intrinsic capacity, are thereby able to give rise to correspondingly varied intrinsic capacities in their results. As with phenomena bound to the desire realm, so too with those bound to the form or formless realms, or unbound to any of the three. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of differentiated capacity, the cause of fixed distinction is set forth.

items.title: The Cause of Concomitant Action: All the Other Causes, Working as One

items.zh: 依和合因依處，施設同事因。所以者何？要由獲得自生和合故，欲繫法生。如欲繫法，如是色、無色繫及不繫法亦爾。如生和合，如是得、成、辦、用和合亦爾。是故依和合依處，施設同事因。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of conjunction that the cause of concomitant action is set forth. Why is this? Because it is only through obtaining the conjunction proper to its own arising that a phenomenon bound to the desire realm arises at all. As with a phenomenon bound to the desire realm, so too with one bound to the form or formless realms, or unbound to any of the three. As with the conjunction proper to arising, so too with the conjunction proper to attainment, establishment, completion, and use. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of conjunction, the cause of concomitant action is set forth.

items.title: The Causes of Opposition and Non-Opposition: What Blocks a Result, and What Lets It Through

items.zh: 依障礙因依處，施設相違因。所以者何？由欲繫法將得生，若障礙現前便不得生。如欲繫法，如是色、無色繫及不繫法亦爾。如生，如是得、成、辦、用亦爾。是故依障礙依處，施設相違因。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of obstruction that the cause of opposition is set forth. Why is this? Because when a phenomenon bound to the desire realm is about to arise, if an obstruction is present, it fails to arise at all. As with a phenomenon bound to the desire realm, so too with one bound to the form or formless realms, or unbound to any of the three. As with arising, so too with attainment, establishment, completion, and use. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of obstruction, the cause of opposition is set forth.

items.zh: 依無障礙因依處，施設不相違因。所以者何？由欲繫法將得生，若無障礙現前，爾時便生。如欲繫法，如是色、無色繫及不繫法亦爾。如生，如是得、成、辦、用亦爾。是故依無障礙依處，施設不相違因。
items.en: It is with reference to the locus of the absence of obstruction that the cause of non-opposition is set forth. Why is this? Because when a phenomenon bound to the desire realm is about to arise, if no obstruction is present, it arises at just that time. As with a phenomenon bound to the desire realm, so too with one bound to the form or formless realms, or unbound to any of the three. As with arising, so too with attainment, establishment, completion, and use. It is for this reason that, with reference to the locus of the absence of obstruction, the cause of non-opposition is set forth.

items.zh: 復次，依種子緣依處，施設因緣。依無間滅緣依處，施設等無間緣。依境界緣依處，施設所緣緣。依所餘緣依處，施設增上緣。
items.en: Further, it is with reference to the locus of the seed-condition that the causal condition is set forth. It is with reference to the locus of the condition of uninterrupted cessation that the condition of uninterrupted equivalence is set forth. It is with reference to the locus of the object-condition that the object condition is set forth. It is with reference to whatever remaining condition-loci there may be that the dominant condition is set forth.

items.zh: 復次，依習氣、隨順因緣依處，施設異熟果及等流果。依真實見因緣依處，施設離繫果。依士用因緣依處，施設士用果。依所餘因緣依處，施設增上果。
items.en: Further, it is with reference to the loci of habitual imprint and of conformity, taken as causal condition, that the ripened result and the result of equal outflow are set forth. It is with reference to the locus of genuine insight, taken as causal condition, that the result of release from bondage is set forth. It is with reference to the locus of human effort, taken as causal condition, that the result of human effort is set forth. It is with reference to whatever remaining causal-condition loci there may be that the dominant result is set forth.

items.title: Three Meanings, and the Ten Causes Reduced to Five

items.zh: 復次，順益義是因義，建立義是緣義，成辦義是果義。又建立因有五種相。一、能生因，二、方便因，三、俱有因，四、無間滅因，五、久遠滅因。
items.en: Further, the meaning of favourable benefit is the meaning of cause; the meaning of establishing is the meaning of condition; the meaning of accomplishment is the meaning of result. Further, cause, when established, has five marks: first, the generative cause; second, the auxiliary cause; third, the co-present cause; fourth, the cause of uninterrupted cessation; fifth, the cause long since ceased.

items.zh: 能生因者，謂生起因。方便因者，謂所餘因。俱有因者，謂攝受因一分。如眼於眼識，如是耳等於所餘識。無間滅因者，謂生起因。久遠滅因者，謂牽引因。
items.en: The generative cause is the cause of generation. The auxiliary cause is every remaining cause. The co-present cause is one portion of the cause of inclusion — as the eye is to eye-consciousness, so are the ear and the rest to their corresponding consciousnesses. The cause of uninterrupted cessation is likewise the cause of generation. The cause long since ceased is the cause of impelling.

blocks.text: Today completes the ten causes and locates the four conditions and five results in the fifteen loci. Several of the causes come with memorable examples from our teachers, and two of them carry direct advice for practice: that small goods grow into great ones, and that a single obstruction can block a result one has long prepared.

subs.head: The cause of generation: craving moistens the seed

blocks.text: **The cause of generation** (生起因) rests on the **moistened seed**: "Craving is what moistens; the seed is what is moistened." The treatise quotes a sūtra: "Karma is the cause of the destiny attained; craving is the cause of its actual arising." This is the technical form of Day 5's self-love "moistening" rebirth. Karma alone does not produce a new life; it needs the water of craving.
**The cause of inclusion** (攝受因) is every supporting condition other than the seed. Master Cháng Bǎi: to grow barley you need soil, fertiliser, rain, and sunlight as well as the seed.

**The cause of drawing-forth** (引發因) rests on conformity: a lesser good draws forth a greater good of the same kind. Master Cháng Bǎi's example: in a past life Ānanda gave food so that a novice could memorise scripture; later he gained a flawless memory. Both teachers add that even unwholesome states can draw forth wholesome ones. Venerable Miào Jìng: someone jealous of another's ordination thinks, "I'll do better", ordains, and practises well. Zhìyǐ built on this the teaching that every affliction can become a door to the path.
**The cause of fixed distinction** (定異因) rests on differentiated capacity: each kind of cause yields its own kind of result. Master Cháng Bǎi: a barley seed produces barley, never wheat.

**The cause of concomitant action** (同事因) is all the other causes working as one. **The cause of opposition** (相違因) is whatever obstructs a result: "if an obstruction is present, it fails to arise". Master Cháng Bǎi's example is sobering: someone who has prepared for rebirth in the Pure Land is provoked at the moment of death by an unfilial son; anger arises, the rebirth fails, and he may even fall lower. (Compare Day 4: what is in the mind at death matters.) **The cause of non-opposition** (不相違因) is the absence of such obstruction.

Each condition has its locus: the causal condition on the seed; the condition of immediate succession on uninterrupted cessation; the object condition on the object; the dominant condition on the rest. Master Cháng Bǎi: mind and mental factors need all four; matter needs only the causal and dominant conditions, since matter has no object and no immediately-preceding moment of the same kind in that sense.

The **ripened result** (異熟果) and the **result of equal outflow** (等流果) rest on habitual imprint and conformity: karma ripens into a body and life of a different kind, while habits produce results like themselves (a generous person becomes more generous). The **result of release from bondage** (離繫果) rests on genuine insight: nirvāṇa is the "result" of insight not because insight produces it but because insight removes what hid it. The **result of human effort** (士用果) rests on action, and the **dominant result** (增上果) on the rest.

The ten causes can be grouped as five: the generative cause (the cause of generation) and the auxiliary cause (the other nine), and so on. Both teachers: "apart from the cause of generation, the other nine are all called auxiliary causes." The two lists are ways of seeing the same causal process from different angles. Tomorrow's reading adds a further grouping and seven marks every real cause must have.

quiz.q: The cause of generation rests on the moistened seed. What sūtra line does the text quote?
options: "Karma is the cause of the destiny attained, craving the cause of its actual arising" — craving moistens, the seed is moistened
quiz.why: "Craving is what moistens; the seed is what is moistened … As the sūtra says: karma is the cause of the destiny attained, craving is the cause of its actual arising." Master Cháng Bǎi: "All kinds of karma determine which destiny one is born into; craving makes the result actually arise"; the cause is broad — covering the result-body, mind, and the world — like a seed producing a sprout, and the sprout a stem.

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, what is the cause of inclusion, and what image does he use?
options: every supporting condition other than the seed — like planting barley, which needs soil, fertilizer, rain
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "For anything to arise, all helping conditions other than the seed are called the cause of inclusion"; "to grow barley, you must plant it in soil and have fertilizer, rain, and so on." The text bases it on uninterrupted cessation, object, faculty, function, human effort, and genuine insight. He adds that matter needs no uninterrupted cessation — just the seed and dominant conditions.

quiz.q: The cause of drawing-forth says a small good draws forth a greater. What past deed of Ānanda does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: in a past life he gave food to help a novice memorise scripture — a desire-realm good that later yielded dhāraṇī, a flawless memory
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "In a past life Ānanda gave food so a novice could memorise scripture — a desire-realm good; later he gained dhāraṇī and never forgot what he saw." Both teachers quote the *Lotus Sūtra*, "even one bow of the head — all attain buddhahood": small goods draw forth great ones. Venerable Miào Jìng: the first time is forced; the second is easier.

quiz.q: The cause of fixed distinction rests on differentiated capacity. What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: a barley seed produces barley sprouts, never wheat
quiz.why: "Phenomena bound to the desire realm, having differences in their own intrinsic capacity, are thereby able to give rise to correspondingly varied intrinsic capacities in their results." Master Cháng Bǎi: "A barley seed produces barley sprouts, not wheat"; it matches the Bodhisattva Stage's "cause of fixed difference." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Fixed distinction means determinate, unconfused" — Confucians say a family's good deeds bless its descendants; in Buddhism, one reaps what one sows oneself.

quiz.q: The text says that "if an obstruction is present, it fails to arise" — the cause of opposition. What deathbed example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: someone bound for the Pure Land is provoked at death by an unfilial son; anger arises, rebirth there fails, and he may fall into a lower realm
there are no obstructions at death
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "But just before death an unfilial son appears and defies him; vexation arises, and not only does he fail to reach the Pure Land — he may fall into a lower realm." Venerable Miào Jìng gives the reverse: a wrongdoer, reminded at death that he once recited the *Diamond Sūtra*, feels joy, and the visions of the lower realms vanish; so "we who practice the good must be careful."

quiz.q: According to Master Cháng Bǎi, how many conditions do mental and material phenomena each need to arise?
options: mind and mental factors need all four; matter needs the causal and dominant conditions
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Mind and mental factors need all four conditions; matter needs two — causal and dominant." Venerable Miào Jìng: "So wherever there is mind, all four conditions are present"; the uninterrupted condition is unique to mind — one moment ceases, the next arises.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, on which loci are the ripened and equal-outflow results set forth? And the result of release?
options: ripened and equal-outflow on habitual imprint and conformity; release on genuine insight
ripened on language, release on faculty
quiz.why: "With reference to the loci of habitual imprint and of conformity … the ripened result and the result of equal outflow are set forth. With reference to the locus of genuine insight … the result of release from bondage." Venerable Miào Jìng: "Habitual imprint brings the ripened result; conformity brings the equal-outflow result"; e.g., shortening another's life yields one's own short life.
